name: Ben
bio: Hey, hi, hello! I'm Ben! I'm a digital illustrator from a weird little town in Pennsylvania who loves all things absurd, ridiculous, and generally peculiar. When I'm not drawing suspicious felines or dapper woodland creatures, I'm probably redesigning the packaging for the ninth time and rearranging tiny frames on my desk trying to find the perfect color combo, or explaining to someone why yes, the fox does need that mustache, no, I will not remove it.

name: Erin
bio: Hi, I'm Erin! I'm a New York-based artist, and my work lives somewhere between the real world and a fairytale I'm still writing. Living with chronic illness and pain has shaped how and why I paint. When words weren't enough, I found I could pour everything — the struggle, the longing for rest, the need for softness — into these calming, magical worlds. My art became my own sanctuary first, before it became anyone else's. Through my art, I hope to offer a gentle place to land — for anyone who needs a little solace, a little beauty, and a little touch of magic.

name: Kat Cramer
bio: Hi, I'm Kat! My work is a bold reflection of my visions, brought to life through vibrant color and gesture. I meld the body and nature in my acrylic paintings, drawing on years of gymnastics that taught me strength, balance, and grace — qualities I chase in every branch, bloom, and curve. Each piece is a reflection of the spirituality I find quietly humming beneath the surface of the natural world.

name: Erin Hoffmann
bio: Hi, I'm Erin Hoffmann! I’m a textile designer and illustrator based out of Brooklyn, NY. While my block prints depict everyday items, I find the texture and bold shapes they are created from have you looking at the everyday differently. Each block print I create is unique to itself: sometimes a press adds or misses a mark, the ink bleeds just a little differently, the paper catches the texture in its own way. No two prints are ever truly identical.

name: Melissa
bio: Hi, I'm Melissa! A multidisciplinary artist creating emotionally charged, surreal portraits that explore identity, vulnerability, and the subconscious. Through bold color palettes, distorted figures, and dreamlike symbolism, my work reflects the tension between inner emotion and external perception.

name: Monica
bio: Hi, I’m NYC Mango! My art explores empowerment, sensuality, and the urban landscape, portraying women as bold, captivating forces within cinematic narratives. Inspired by the dramatic allure of film noir and the vibrant pulse of New York City, I paint through the lens of the femme fatale, exploring self-expression and the magnetic tension between beauty and grit that defines the city.

name: Karen Vidals
bio: Unlicensed Karebear, otherwise known as Karen Vidals, is a Mexican-American illustrator born and raised in Upstate New York. She received her bachelor's in illustration at FIT in 2022. Always striving to improve on her craft, Karen continues to draw whatever interests her most. Her main goal as an illustrator is to never stop creating and inspire others.

name: Keemo
bio: Hi, I'm Keemo! I have been making art almost every day for over 35 years. I knew from a very young age that this is what I was going to do with my life and every day since has been working to make this happen. When I was young I learned that making art is a great way to work through all the stuff going on in your head and life. It forces you to be alone with yourself and think about the world and how we all fit into it. Which is exactly what my art is about: exploring who we are, how we all fit into this world and what the heck it all means.

name: Laura Knight
bio: Hi! I'm Laura, the illustrator behind Pancake Press! I'm based in Greenwich Village, and I create digital artwork inspired by everyday moments: from a perfect slice of pizza to a colorful picnic or sunny brunch spread. I'm drawn to familiar objects and places and enjoy reimagining them in a vibrant and playful style. Most of my pieces start as a photo and end up as an illustration, usually with my dog keeping me company in the process.

name: Dani
bio: Hi, I'm Dani! My world is built out of clashing pinks and purples and acid greens, electric platform boots with spikes that mean business, hair that curls like smoke, monsters perched on shoulders like familiars who've never once been good influences. I love the in-between — cute and unsettling living in the same frame, glamour and gore holding hands. A crown made of brains. A creature with a hundred staring eyes and bone earrings. A girl with mismatched eyes who looks like she knows something you don't. I draw to make things feel strange, electric, a little dangerous, and a little bit beautiful anyway.

name: Courtney Stanley
bio: Hi, I'm Courtney! A pen and ink artist living in Cleveland, Tennessee. Art has been part of my life since I was a kid dreaming of becoming an artist and somehow, that dream stuck. These days, my pen finds its way to florals and still lifes, often drawn from memory: the gardens, kitchen tables, and quiet corners that shaped my childhood between Georgia and Tennessee. Each piece is a small love letter to where I come from.

name: Margo Moore
bio: Hi, I'm Margo Moore! Raised in Poland and now rooted in Ridgewood, Queens — a community I've come to call home for the way it resists the city's mutated sameness and stays unpretentious, gritty, and real. My work spans abstract and figurative pieces, portraits, caricatures, letter art, and the meticulous pen-and-ink drawings that capture the textured, overlapping life of New York. I draw inspiration from daily moments, from the architecture and chaos of the city around me, sketching during my commute. At the heart of my practice is an interest in preserving the character of NYC.

name: Mario
bio: Hi, I'm Mario! I'm a self-taught artist based in Brooklyn, working with acrylic and watercolor. My work often starts with something concrete, a structure, a body, a piece of construction, but I blur it, break it apart, and let it drift into abstraction. I am not interested in painting things exactly as they are but more focus on the emotion they carry, the texture, and energy they bring into space. I am inspired by vibrant color combinations, unexpected imagination, and the relationship between the micro and macro, how the smallest moments of everyday life can reflect something much larger and unseen.

name: Flora Hu
bio: Hi, I’m Flora Hu! I’m an artist and designer from France, now based in NYC. I work primarily in pen and ink, drawing everyday objects with fine linework and bold shadows to capture the reflective surfaces of glass and metal. Drawn to objects shaped by use and repetition, my work explores the beauty of ordinary things through light, texture, and form.

name: Ali
bio: Hi, I'm Ali! I'm an artist who is curious about everything, and always has been. I was the kid who scribbled on everything and the adult who still doodles on any piece of paper you put in front of me. Somewhere along the way I also developed a serious love for being surrounded by interesting, beautiful things, so now I'm combining that with my art and doodles.

name: Melissa Hallbrook
bio: Hi, I'm Melissa Hallbrook! I aim to capture the likeness of my subject matter in a way that not only exhibits a tangible sense of representation, but also the spirit or internal character of what I observe. I use realism stylistically in an attempt to tell stories about people, to show not only their physical form but also their essence. My work intends not only to “preserve” human beings in a particular time and place, but also to protect a lineage of practical techniques that seem to be fast disappearing in our modern world. I consider myself an anthropologist of method, learning everything I can about time-honored materials and applications. My pieces aim to create visually captivating works that form a satisfying blend of traditional and contemporary sensibility.

name: Joseph P. Riccio
bio: Hi, I'm Joseph P. Riccio, known as C1MAH (Clarity in Mind & Heart)! A New York native who blends faces, colors, and textures inspired by NYC street art. My pieces reflect life's challenges, emotions, and growth through mixed media, while my moniker reflects my pursuit of peace, love, and self-discovery. Rooted in meditation, my art carries uplifting messages that encourage others to dream, aspire, and embrace positivity. I've left my mark across NYC through murals, hand-painted custom apparel, and large-scale vinyl installations. I'm the first artist to work with Mystry Mart, having painted their very first machine. Lately, I've been pushing my work into a new dimension, creating layered sculptural pieces that blend street art with craftsmanship. Each piece starts as laser-cut forms that I spray-paint, stack, and assemble by hand, layer by layer. What begins as a flat sheet evolves into a bold, dimensional composition where words, symbols, and stories seem to float off the surface.

name: Michael O'Malley
bio: Hi, I'm Michael O'Malley! I started painting frogs because I wanted to paint something fun. These frogs are soldiers because life asks us to fight for ourselves sometimes, and they're kings because surviving that fight is its own kind of crown. Healing is rarely sudden — it happens slowly, one day at a time, but the important part is continuing forward. One frog turned to two, two turned to three, and next thing you know we had a hundred frogs, and somewhere along the way I really started to enjoy these little soldiers and kings. And it's true — anyone could paint these. That's exactly why I chose them. The simplicity isn't an accident; it's the point. Frogs are easy, unpretentious, a little goofy — just like the people they represent, carrying weight nobody else can see while still showing up, still smiling, still moving. Because no matter what, we keep going.

name: Peyton Sachs
bio: Hi, I'm Peyton Sachs! I don't sketch anything out before I start, I just stand in front of a blank canvas and let whatever's inside me find its way to the surface. I never went to art school, never learned the rules, so I don't have anything to unlearn either; it's just me, some paint, and whatever brushes I've got lying around. My work isn't about looking good or being technically right, it's about being honest. I've lived in Vegas, LA, and now New York, and I think that's given me a strange front-row seat to how people perform happiness while quietly falling apart, and that tension is what keeps showing up in my paintings whether I plan it or not. I'm still figuring out what my style even is, and honestly I hope I never fully figure it out. The second this stops feeling raw and starts feeling like a formula is the second I'll know I've lost the thing that made me pick up a brush in the first place.

name: Tannin Arceo
bio: Hi, I'm Tannin Arceo! A Filipino-American illustrator focused on environmental illustration that lingers in light, shadow, and liminal spaces. My work is shaped by my queer identity and Asian-American upbringing, which comes through in a wide-ranging, often saturated color palette and in the small references to childhood toys and memories I tuck into every scene.

name: Becca
bio: Hi, I'm Becca, also known as TinyBS! TinyBS is unapologetically fun ceramics. Ageless. Genderless. It's porcelain for the 21st century. My ceramics are informed by my Mexican-American childhood and my Brooklyn adulthood. Each tiny work of art is a small gem of authentic and often irreverent self in a portable jewelry form. Hand formed and illustrated with 22k gold in Gowanus, Brooklyn.

name: Victoria
bio: Hi, I'm Victoria! I create my whimsical urban illustrations from my bedroom studio in New Jersey, drawing inspiration from the people, places, and shows around me — it all finds its way into my art. Alongside creating, I work as an art instructor, passionate about helping others tap into their creativity, especially kids, for whom I feel a strong calling. My goal is to create a space where young artists feel accepted, supported, and encouraged to explore their passions — helping them feel like they belong and know their creativity truly matters.

name: Zoee Xiao
bio: Hi, I'm Zoee Xiao! A painter working primarily in watercolor and acrylic, where I blend the minimalist elegance of Eastern aesthetics with the bold, colorful expressiveness of Western styles. I was born and raised in a small southern town in China, where I first learned to paint under the guidance of a sumi-e master, before moving to the United States to study animation at the University of Pennsylvania and later working as a software engineer in the gaming industry. My love for art never faded during those tech years, and in 2022 I left my job to paint full-time. My work draws from childhood memories, reinterpreting them through a fantastical, playful lens to evoke nostalgia and joy, and to invite viewers back to the simplicity and wonder so easily lost in adulthood.

name: Amber
bio: Hi! I'm Amber, an experimental photographic artist creating whimsical, nature-inspired works with a touch of magic. My process is primarily based in photography, with an emphasis on alternative processes like film soup, cyanotype, lumen printing and scanography. I also shoot 35mm film, instant film and digital formats. I take every opportunity I can to let my curiosity get the best of me! “What if?” is a question that I love to ask and answer. Experimentation, trying new things and playing with new-to-me mediums and methods is an important part of my artistic process. I love that experimentation asks me to step out of my comfort zone, let go of perfection and enjoy the grounded, human experience of trial and error. Much of my work combines nature's inherent beauty with surreal, whimsical elements to create visuals that feel like they belong to another world, but are very much a part of this one. I like to infuse as much joy and fun as I can into my pieces. Through my art, I hope to show others the magic on our planet that's hiding in plain sight and that a brighter, more colorful world is always possible.

name: Corrine
bio: Hi, I'm Corrine! A Maryland-based artist working in ink, paint, and digital mediums. My work draws from the shifting beauty of nature and the elegance of the feminine form, often blending fine detail with bold, abstract composition. I seek to create pieces that invite the viewers into a world both familiar and surreal, where strength and softness exist side by side.

name: Doug Sandelin
bio: Hi, I'm Doug Sandelin! Art is like life: a series of mistakes in the process of correction. Creativity is a mysterious process of the mind generated by dreams, and if the mystery of dreams is overly defined objectively, then I fear it will die. Creativity is beyond physical—a dream state of human reality, a meta-reality that goes beyond what we usually perceive.

name: Chao
bio: Hi, I'm Chao! These ceramics are inspired by the beauty of nature—animals, flowers, and the quiet charm of rustic and modern design. Each piece is made to feel warm, simple, and a little bit special.

name: China Lamont
bio: Hi, I'm China Lamont! My art is a deep exploration of womanhood, identity, and the quiet power that lives within. I work primarily with bold, saturated color as my emotional language — blues, earth tones, magentas, and golds that speak before the image even registers. My figures are never fully exposed; eyes are covered, heads are absent, faces are fragmented, because I believe the most profound parts of a person exist beyond what's visible on the surface. I'm drawn to the tension between the natural and the constructed — butterflies and flowers colliding with grids and geometric planes to reflect how women are constantly navigating freedom within constraint. Ultimately, my work is an invitation to sit with that complexity, to find beauty in transformation, and to recognize the strength in simply existing as you are.

name: Diana Teeter
bio: Hi, I'm Diana Teeter and welcome to Dianaland! I paint cute animals doing silly little things — a pigeon who drinks coffee and wears Timbs or a rat wearing a crown made of a MetroCard while eating pizza. It's very NYC-based. Sometimes I draw animals in cosplay, and other times more fairytale-like animals in cloaks, sharing quiet moments with lantern flies and moths. It all started as something whimsical just for me, a way to entertain myself and make myself laugh — but somehow, much to my surprise, other people fell in love with Dianaland too, and now I get to share this strange, tender, funny little world with all of you!

name: Megan
bio: Hi, I'm Megan! A mystical surrealist artist who paints small worlds full of wonder, tucked inside ornate vintage frames where a goose perches proudly atop a golden egg, toadstools glow under a candy-colored sky, and a topiary rabbit seems to breathe against the clouds; drawing on fairytales, nature, magic, and my own childhood imagination, I invite viewers to step into these tiny mystical scenes and write their own stories within them. And because art and compassion go hand in hand for me, I donate a portion of my proceeds to animal rescue and mental health organizations.

name: Mariya
bio: Hi, I'm Mariya! My work lives at the intersection of nightlife, music, and the electric energy of people gathered together in the dark. The world I draw is the world I live in and DJ in — loud, alive, and always just on the edge of something. My illustrations capture the feeling of a room full of bodies moving to a beat, the charged tension of a night that could go anywhere, the intimacy and chaos of the crowd. Whether I'm behind the decks or behind a screen, I'm chasing the same thing: that feeling.

name: Ethan Minsker
bio: Hi, I'm Ethan Minsker! My visual art revolves around the concept of upcycling, where I breathe new life into what might otherwise be considered trash. Working primarily in mixed media, I incorporate materials such as papier-maché, cardboard from shipping boxes, cans, plastic bottles, chapsticks, and a variety of other discarded containers. I aim to transform these overlooked and discarded objects into something precious once more. The pieces presented here span different collections but are unified by themes of childlike wonder, tinged with a touch of melancholy. Through this interplay of joy and sadness, I invite viewers to reconsider the value of what we so easily throw away.

name: Shushanik Karapetyan
bio: Hi, I'm Shushanik Karapetyan! A New York-based artist born in Yerevan, Armenia, whose paintings live in the quiet, luminous space between sky and earth, color and feeling, structure and flow. My work is deeply informed by my practice as a Gestalt psychotherapist — I approach painting the way I approach presence, with attunement and responsiveness to personal experience and the environment around me. I'm drawn to sunsets, seasonal shifts, and the vivid colors of flowers I encounter on my walks, and these impressions weave themselves into layered, horizon-based compositions that explore contrast, balance, and what I think of as the "contact-boundary" — that tender space where we connect with and separate from others and ourselves. Some boundaries in my paintings blur softly into one another, others hold a sharp, definitive edge, mirroring the push and pull of being human.

name: Ashley Debeer
bio: Hi, I'm Ashley Debeer! A visual artist whose practice thrives on tension and contrast, most notably through color. Drawing inspiration from the natural world— seashells, clouds, the night sky, and native flowers— I translate these elements into bold compositions where vibrant colors collide in unexpected ways. Rejecting conventional norms, I forge a visual language that resists structure and embraces raw instinct.

name: Jessica
bio: Hi, I'm Jessica! My collection is drawn from my oil and watercolor paintings — small sections lifted from larger canvases, each one a closer look at something I felt was worth pausing for. I think of every painting as a portrait. Not of a person, but of a peony, a poppy, a flower so familiar you might walk past it without a second glance. I want to give that second glance back to people. I'm drawn to the quiet architecture of petals, the way light moves through translucent white, the deep almost-black of a flower that refuses to be ordinary. Whether I'm painting the soft blush of a peony or the inky drama of a midnight bloom, I'm studying the same thing — the intricacy nature builds without ever trying to impress anyone. Through this work, I hope to translate something of nature's peaceful, healing energy onto paper and canvas, and from there, into the everyday spaces where people live. My paintings are my way of bringing the charm of the outdoors a little closer to home.

name: Jenny Walker
bio: Hi, I'm Jenny Walker! An artist and librarian, and both of those things are more connected than they might seem, because everything I make is driven by a deep curiosity about the stories we tell ourselves and others, and the ways those narratives shape how we understand the world. Working in ink, acrylic, charcoal, and monotype printmaking, I create intimate works that blur the boundary between painting and drawing, finding the emotional charge hiding inside traditional subjects like portraiture and landscape. I'm a process-oriented artist, which means the materials themselves are always part of the conversation, and I follow them as much as I lead them.

name: Jet Takayama
bio: Hi, I'm Jet Takayama! I'm a mixed Asian-American multi-disciplinary artist living on Lenape land, also known as Philadelphia. I was born in South Carolina on the land of the Cherokee and Congaree peoples and raised near the Congaree River amongst flowers and birdsong, spending most of my childhood sitting in trees and barefoot in the grass — and that deep love for the natural world and the beings that live in it never left me. I grew up surrounded by my great-grandfather's vivid landscape paintings and started daydreaming and drawing young, and my work today echoes all of it, combining depictions of flora and fauna with fantasy and myth, the real world and the imagined one always beautifully tangled together. I aim to make work that reminds you that there is always a little bit of wild magic left to be found.

name: Erynne Byrd-Quigtar
bio: Hi, I'm Erynne Byrd-Quigtar! A fine and digital artist whose work celebrates the rich and powerful experience of Black culture. Through vibrant colors and dynamic textures, I bring to life the depth, beauty, and complexity of Black identity. My art serves as a visual tribute to resilience, joy, and the multifaceted narratives within the Black community, offering a unique and compelling perspective on cultural expression.

name: Lizzy Itzkowitz
bio: Hi, I'm Lizzy! I'm an illustrator, cartoonist, pattern designer, and animated GIF-maker from New York City. I was diagnosed with ADHD in my teen years and have been trying to navigate the world ever since (mostly with the help of google maps). When I'm not creating stuff, I spend my time training to break the world record for most nostril flares in under one minute (I'm pretty close to beating it I swear). I love drawing happy things, bright colors, making people laugh, hot dogs, and I'm on a mission to make the world suck less!

name: Lucy-Kate
bio: Hi, I'm Lucy-Kate! I came back to art in my thirties after years away, working now across acrylic, mixed media, and sculpture. My paintings bring together animals, plants, crystals, and bones, pairing the wild with the precious in ways that feel a little surreal, a little whimsical, always rendered in saturated color. At the heart of it is reverence: for the strange beauty of the natural world, for the creatures and minerals and small rituals most people walk past, and for the wonder of looking closely enough to really see them.

name: Jessica Fisher
bio: Hi, I'm Jessica Fisher! A painter working in oil, and everything I make begins with confession. My practice is about making visible what resists being spoken. I bring the viewer in close; faces fill the frame, eyes hold attention, and the space between subject and observer collapses until looking becomes something mutual and unsettling.

name: Vanessa Summers
bio: Hi, my name is Vanessa Summers! I'm a Queens-based artist who pours my imagination into every piece I create. I dedicate my work to developing characters and stories through a fantastical lens, especially artwork that represents myself and other BIPOC individuals within the fantasy genre. My love for fantasy began when I was young. I always found comfort in escaping into the worlds of movies and books, but I constantly noticed the lack of people of color within them. Because of that, I decided to create my own worlds and characters, worlds where Black and Brown people are just as present as anyone else. My work focuses on the whimsy and wonder of fantasy, depicting magical beings and fantasy races with more inclusive skin tones and facial features. I create spaces where BIPOC characters can be heroes, villains, strange, soft, powerful, possess magic, wield swords, and everything in between. In my world, fantasy is as limitless as imagination itself, and everyone has a place within it.

name: Samuel Jay
bio: Hi, I'm Samuel Jay! I play the harmonica. Have for most of my life. And I paint the way I play — by feel, by breath, by something that moves through me. My figures dance, they strut, they leap. They are always in motion because stillness was never something I understood. My subjects are all performers. They are all on stage. For me, the canvas has always been my theater.

name: scribbz_sqribbles
bio: Hi, I'm Sqribbz, and I have a tiny obsession with scribble-scrabbling faces from time to time. Every face I encounter hones a personality... and I'm especially drawn to the ones that tilt a little, droop a little, squint at me like they're hiding a tiny secret. I scribble them with my pastels the moment they wander into my mind, the moment I remember a fleeting face I've seen before... usually uninvited, usually mid eye roll. It's often forgotten that every face we glimpse carries something. A past they half-remember, a mood they pretend they don't feel, a joke tucked behind a crooked line, a splash of color that refuses to behave. I don't invent their stories - I just scribble them out. People overlook faces all the time. A face is just a face until it becomes special, until it belongs to someone they love, hate, miss, care for, or recognize. I stretch a cheekbone, bend a nose, drag a line until it wiggles. I poke, twist, pull, scratch, dissolve, and scribble... stripping away the surface until, somewhere between the scribbles and scrabbles, what remains is the soul.

name: Tanner Bosma
bio: Hi, I'm Tanner! A rain and cityscape painter based in Brooklyn, originally from Michigan with a degree in Art Education, now pursuing painting full-time and so grateful you're here. My work lives in the cinematic, moody, after-dark corners of the city. I aim to create a beautiful tension between solitude and urban life, a place where time slows, light lingers, and the city pulses with a quiet and almost melancholy energy that I find endlessly beautiful about New York at night in the rain.

name: Toni
bio: Hi, I'm Toni! I'm an artist and musician whose work lives somewhere between dreams and nightmares — childlike and colorful, a little surreal, where things don't always have to make full sense but the natural world always finds its way through. My subjects are often myself and the nature I love, the quiet magic of the living world around us rendered in bold, saturated color that feels like a memory you can almost but not quite place. I want people who step into my art to feel like they've wandered into a backroom of their childhood perception of the world, that strange and tender place where everything was vivid and alive and new and a little bit strange.

name: Emily Veldman
bio: Hi, I'm Emily Veldman! A Los Angeles-based artist and illustrator whose colorful, narrative-driven work across painting, sculpture, and mixed media is rooted in my experience living with Generalized Anxiety Disorder — building visual sanctuaries where yarn becomes furniture, felt becomes food, and imagined worlds filled with personified animals and whimsical textures offer a gentle, playful contrast to the chaos anxiety can create. These aren't just escapist spaces — they're alternate realities where anxiety doesn't dictate the terms, and where I hope viewers find their own small moment of calm, delight, or recognition. Ultimately, my work is about care: for self, for others, and for the imaginative inner worlds that help keep us afloat.

name: Mads
bio: Hi, I'm Mads! I am a queer multimedia ceramicist based out of Arizona, who uses critters real and imaginary as inspiration for my pottery. Carving through the flat surface, I illustrate my characters with unique bodies and personalities. My goal is to bring humor, love, and joy with my little clay creations! My critters are a little goofy, a little wild, always a little bit themselves — and that's exactly the point. I want people to look at these odd, colorful little creatures and feel a little more permission to be odd and colorful too.

name: Zheyi Zhang
bio: Hi, I'm Zheyi Zhang! Born in 1975 in Guilin, China, now a New York City artist whose practice spans painting, works on paper, installation, and public art, rooted in a deep examination of the relationships between time, culture, and space. When I arrived in New York, it was the MetroCard that opened the city to me — a small rectangle of access that allowed me to travel, discover, and fall in love with every neighborhood and corner of this place — and so I began painting my experiences directly onto them, turning these everyday transit cards into miniature canvases that capture what I saw and felt as a newcomer finding his footing in one of the world's most electric cities. What started as an intimate personal practice has since grown into something much larger, inspiring a devoted cult following and an extensive international exhibition career spanning the US, Asia, Europe, and Australia — including three solo shows in New York City galleries alone!

name: Ashlee Fears
bio: Hi, I'm Ashlee Fears, a South Dakota-based artist working primarily in watercolor, ink, and acrylic. Originally from Illinois, I earned my BFA in Studio Art from Illinois State University, where I focused on intaglio and printmaking. Since moving to Western South Dakota in 2017, I've found endless inspiration in the landscapes of the Black Hills. My work is colorful, playful, and inspired by the simple joy of looking at art. For me, creating has always been therapeutic, offering a way to express feelings and ideas that can't always be put into words. I'm currently working toward bringing my art into the world of surface design and hope to one day see my work on store shelves.

name: Ashley Fimbel
bio: Hello! I'm Ashley Fimbel, the artist and creator behind Art Fimbel, a playful cat-centric brand inspired by my lifelong love for cats! Based in New York's Capital District, I create fun cat-themed items including art prints, polymer clay keychains, pins, stickers, and even a coloring book! Every piece that I create is made with care and personality, often inspired by my own three cats, who make the perfect muses. Whether you're a cat lover, a sticker enthusiast, or just someone who appreciates a little cuteness and whimsy, I hope my creations bring a smile to your face!

name: chaotic_bell
bio: Bio coming soon.

name: Emye
bio: I'm Emye, an abstract artist and creative alchemist blending color, texture, and intuitive energy into functional art. My work explores the cosmic, mystical, and emotional through watercolor, acrylic, digital layering, and sculptural textures, creating pieces that connect with nature, soul, and self.

name: Kelvonnah
bio: Hi, I'm Kelvonnah. I'm an Arizona-native artist and the creator behind Fly Girl Prints. My art is inspired by the beauty of the desert, African American culture, natural hair, and all things fly. Through my work, I love celebrating individuality, culture, beauty, and self-expression. Each piece is created to bring personality into a space while reflecting the things that inspire me and the world around me. My collection features bold, eye-catching artwork that invites you to embrace your own style and make your space feel like you.

name: Kara
bio: Hi, I'm Kara, a New York-based illustrator and visual artist inspired by lively color, thoughtful composition, and rich texture. I see art-making as a process of asking and answering questions, always approaching the work as a student. With a background in multimedia art, experience working with various institutions, and studies in Fine Art at Pratt Institute, I bring together different mediums and perspectives to create my visual language. My work explores the imagination and the connections between humanity, society, nature, and the fantastical world of the subconscious.

name: Jessica Lou
bio: I'm Jessica Lou, an independent artist based in Brooklyn, New York. I love to reimagine Chinese culture in a new and cute way through a variety of art mediums, including block-printing, graphic design, risograph printing, and digital illustration. My work resonates with children, teens, and young adults by capturing the nostalgia of growing up as a third-culture kid. I have spent the past 3 years selling my work online and at in-person popups.

name: marymakingmoves
bio: Bio coming soon.

name: Jackie
bio: Hi, I'm Jackie, the artist and creator behind Midnight City Tarot. My journey began with a tarot reading that gave me a resounding “yes” when I asked if I should move to New York City. I took the leap, arriving in Brooklyn with a one-way ticket, an open heart, and a deep trust in where life was leading me. Over the years, New York and tarot became my greatest teachers, inspiring me to create a deck that reflected my own journey through the city. I illustrated each card with bright colors, playful imagery, and vibrant city scenes set against a midnight sky, exploring themes of intuition, possibility, transformation, and the unknown. Midnight City Tarot was born from that spirit of following your intuition and finding magic in the in-between. My work is created to make tarot feel approachable, relatable, and joyful, whether you're a lifelong reader or picking up a deck for the very first time.

name: Min Park
bio: Hi, I'm Min Park, a Korean artist and designer based in Brooklyn, New York. Having grown up in South Korea and later moved to New York, I found myself living between two cultures and two worlds, an experience that deeply shapes my work. My practice explores identity, memory, belonging, and the feeling of being caught between different versions of yourself. I draw inspiration from everyday experiences, dreams, memories, and emotions that can be difficult to put into words. Working across painting, drawing, illustration, and installation, I use watercolor, ink, pencil, translucent paper, and fabric to create soft, layered, and dreamlike imagery. Through my work, I hope to turn personal experiences of displacement and belonging into something others can connect with in their own way.

name: Steven Levin
bio: Hi, I'm Steven Levin. My work explores portraiture through a playful, surreal, and sometimes eerie lens. I paint small, expressive images of faces, eyes, mouths, animals, flowers, and imagined worlds, often placing them inside ornate vintage-style frames. I'm drawn to the contrast between the beauty and nostalgia of the frames and the strange, unexpected imagery within them, creating little worlds that feel both familiar and otherworldly.

name: symbolicinteractionstudio

name: Abby
bio: Hi, I'm Abby! I'm an animation director and illustrator working in digital and traditional media. My work includes Nonna, an internationally award-winning stop-motion short film, and I'm the recipient of the 2019 S.P.A.C.E. minicomics award. My work has been featured in film festivals and galleries around the world. When I'm not creating, you can find me eating fresh cannoli, wandering through the woods, or cuddling with my two very silly cats.

name: artbyfaneshafabre
bio: Bio coming soon.

name: C.G. Hall
bio: Hi, I'm C.G. Hall, a visual artist exploring the intersection of sacred geometry, mythology, and human consciousness. Working across acrylic, oil, ink, graphite, and mixed media, I combine anatomical forms, cosmic imagery, mathematics, and esoteric philosophy to explore the hidden patterns underlying nature, spirituality, and perception. My work invites viewers to look beyond the visible and reflect on the unseen structures that shape reality, meaning, and the human experience.

name: Delphine Le Goff
bio: Hi, I'm Delphine Le Goff, a Paris-born artist based in New York City's East Village. My work celebrates the beauty in everyday life, from flowers and city landmarks to unexpected objects and imaginary spaces. I find inspiration in the world around me, turning ordinary moments into unique works of art.

name: hibyetiles
bio: Bio coming soon.

name: Kelly
bio: Hi! I'm Kelly, and I create playful worlds full of personality. I'm a Philly-based illustrator and graphic designer who loves bringing ideas to life through characters, storytelling, and moments of whimsy. From children's products and educational materials to murals, games, and community spaces, I create artwork that feels thoughtful, welcoming, and full of whimsy.

name: Kyle Wolffking
bio: Hi! My name is Kyle Wolffking and I'm an illustrator working in Chicago. I believe that illustration can captivate the imagination of children of all ages — including adults! — by telling immersive stories. Humans are storytellers by nature and the way I tell stories is through my art.

name: lazi.sooz
bio: Hi, I'm the artist behind LAZI SOOZ! With a background in computer science and a love for all things creative, I started LAZI SOOZ in 2022 to bring my passion for art back to life. I create playful illustrations and goodies inspired by kawaii animals, my pets, Asian food, and the tech world. My style is all about fluffy characters, round shapes, pastel colors, and a little bit of cheeky humor!

name: megtruong.art
bio: Bio coming soon.

name: Amy Salomone
bio: Hi, I'm Amy Salomone, an artist passionate about bringing scientific concepts to life through visual storytelling. What began as a gift for a friend grew into an exploration of evolution, natural selection, animal behavior, perception, and our place in the universe. Through my work, I hope to challenge perspectives, spark curiosity, and inspire people to see themselves and the world around them in a new light.

name: Nethery
bio: Hi, I'm Nethery, an illustrator and storyteller inspired by the world of comic books. I create self-published comics, children's books, and illustrated ceramics, exploring storytelling through a variety of mediums, including animation, pottery, printmaking, and watercolor. My work is driven by curiosity and a love for experimenting with different art forms, always looking for new ways to bring stories and characters to life.

name: Rosanna
bio: Hi, I'm Rosanna, a New York-based painter inspired by the colorful, adventurous lives of the people around me. My work explores contemporary culture through vibrant paintings of travel, beauty, self-care, tarot, magic, and everyday moments. I'm also the artist behind Ucampesina Flowerchild, a handmade jewelry shop inspired by my Dominican roots and New York upbringing. My approach to art is eclectic and unconstrained, allowing me to follow whatever sparks my curiosity.

name: sara_antoinette_martin
bio: Bio coming soon.

name: Cindy Sun
bio: Hey there! I'm Cindy Sun, the illustrator behind Sunnyside Studios. I am currently based in the vibrant neighbourhood of downtown Toronto, ON (no, I don't live in Sunnyside haha). The name “Sunnyside Studios” is inspired by my last name “Sun” and my desire to bring more sunshine into the world through my art. My passion lies in drawing adorable cats and capturing the simple joys of life, from delicious food and blooming flowers to charming cafes. My goal is to infuse happiness into each piece, brightening your day with every creation.

name: Maureen McAfee
bio: Hi, I'm Maureen McAfee, a Brooklyn-based ceramicist and illustrator inspired by vintage artwork, miniatures, and tableware. My work explores our connection to the objects we collect and the memories, stories, and meanings they hold. Originally from Massachusetts, I spent my early childhood on Cape Cod, and the seaside remains a lasting source of inspiration for my creative practice.

name: Thomas Lauro
bio: Bio coming soon.

name: Kamila Zmrzla
bio: Hi, I'm Kamila Zmrzla, a Brooklyn-based self-taught artist inspired by my Czech upbringing, folklore, and the vibrant characters of everyday life. Working across painting, ink, watercolor, textiles, and found objects, I create colorful, richly patterned compositions exploring nature, femininity, and the beauty of the unconventional. My pigeon paintings blend the charm of these familiar city birds with the personalities of the people you might encounter on the streets of New York City. Drawing on my Czech roots and love for expressive forms and vivid colors, I give these urban characters a playful, human quality, inviting viewers to find humor, familiarity, and beauty in the everyday.

name: Yushin Kato
bio: Hi, I’m Yushin Kato, a bicultural, interdisciplinary artist and designer based in Brooklyn, New York. I work primarily with ink, graphite, and gouache, using abstract and symbolic botanical imagery to explore the elegance and intelligence of natural forms and metaphysical realms. My creative process is intuitive, balancing precision with spontaneity, and structure with surrender. Through my work, I invite viewers to reflect on the beauty of the natural world and its intrinsic connection to our everyday lives.

name: Callie Danae Hirsch
bio: Hi, I'm Callie! I grew up in the mountainous region of Rockland County, New York, and now live in Brooklyn. My work blends wildlife and city life, drawing inspiration from nature's energy, spontaneity, and mysteries. Through playful compositions, earthy colors, and organic forms, I explore the stories hidden within the natural world. I work across a variety of mediums, including ink on paper, oil on canvas, and acrylic on mannequins. My recent work features iridescent acrylics on black etching paper, where individual dots become sources of energy and cells merge, separate, and evolve into new forms of life.

name: Em Spitler
bio: Hi, I'm Em! I'm an illustrator who loves embracing the weird and nonsensical, challenging my own perfectionism along the way. My work features misshapen animals, unexpected color combinations, and playful textures. I create using everything from stubby colored pencils and well-loved paint tubes to smudgy pastels and my trusty Apple Pencil. When I'm not illustrating, you can usually find me cuddling my cat Meemoo, biking around the neighborhood, or tinkering in the garden.

name: Maham Sarwar
bio: Hi, I'm Maham! I'm an artist and designer exploring abstract expression through painting. My work challenges traditional notions of art and beauty, using color, composition, and form to evoke emotion and wonder. Drawing inspiration from my background in textile design and South Asian culture, I use the canvas to share my experiences, perspectives, and the way I see the world.

name: nycartbyme

name: breadslug
bio: Bread Slug is a NYC based multidisciplinary artist turning leftover bread into one of a kind, surreal artworks. Every day is a new bread and every bread is a new crisis.

name: Lihua Chen
bio: Hi, I'm Lihua! I'm a New York-based artist and freelance writer with over two decades of experience in the creative field. My practice spans painting, video, and public art, exploring the emotions and deeper meanings that lie beneath the surface. My work has been exhibited internationally in cities including Beijing, London, Berlin, and New York, and I've created large-scale public installations and interdisciplinary projects that bring together art, design, music, and performance.

name: Kat Buckles
bio: Hi, I’m Kat Buckles, also known as Fotowanderex. I am a fine art photographer using experimental methods to create surreal and magical images. All of my art is created in-camera, involving techniques like multiple exposure and slow shutter speed. I enjoy creating unexpected images which juxtapose different themes or turn ordinary objects upside down. I strive to see our surroundings in wild and otherworldly ways, challenging my viewers to join me in finding enchantment, peculiar beauty, and strange poetry all around us.

name: Fish Lee
bio: Hi, I'm Fish Lee (or Sunny)! I'm an artist inspired by animals, storytelling, and the playful possibilities of imagination. My work transforms land creatures into whimsical water beings, exploring how nature connects, contrasts, and surprises us.

name: Lindsey Cherek Waller
bio: Hi, I’m Lindsey! I’m a queer, non-binary artist based in Charlotte, North Carolina. Through portraiture and still life paintings, I explore pleasure, joy, and a future beyond binaries. My work encourages people to take up space, embrace play, and imagine new possibilities for a better world. I’ve collaborated with brands like Urban Outfitters, Hulu, and Paramount Pictures, and exhibited my work across the US.
